record.original_question: For every even integer k, prove or refute that the layered pattern of length k with layers (1, 2, 2, ..., 2, 2, 1) is the most avoided pattern among all patterns of length k.

evidence.quote: For example, a conjecture of Kézdy and Snevily [18, Conj. 9.10] that has not been refuted is that for patterns of even length k the most avoided pattern is the one with layers (1, 2, 2, . . . , 2, 2, 1).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. Given a permutation $\sigma \in S_n$ and a permutation (pattern) $\tau \in S_k$ with $k\le n$, an occurrence of $\tau$ in $\sigma$ is a $k$-tuple of indices $1\le i_1<i_2<\cdots<i_k\le n$ such that the values $\sigma(i_1),\sigma(i_2),\dots,\sigma(i_k)$ appear in the same relative order as $\tau(1),\tau(2),\dots,\tau(k)$. Let $c(\tau,\sigma)$ denote the number of occurrences of $\tau$ in $\sigma$, and define
$$\delta(\tau,\sigma)=\frac{c(\tau,\sigma)}{\binom{n}{k}}.$$
The packing density of $\tau$ is
$$\mathrm{pd}(\tau)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\max_{\sigma\in S_n}\delta(\tau,\sigma).$$

A layered permutation with layer sequence $(\ell_1,\ell_2,\dots,\ell_r)$ (positive integers with $\ell_1+\cdots+\ell_r=k$) is the permutation in $S_k$ obtained by concatenating $r$ consecutive blocks, where the $i$-th block consists of $\ell_i$ entries arranged in decreasing order, and the blocks are placed so that all entries of block $i$ are smaller than all entries of block $i+1$. Equivalently it is a permutation that avoids both $231$ and $312$.

Call a pattern $\tau\in S_k$ "most avoided of length $k$" if $\mathrm{pd}(\tau)$ attains the minimum value of $\mathrm{pd}$ over all $\tau'\in S_k$.

Problem. Prove or disprove: for every even integer $k\ge 2$, the layered pattern of length $k$ with layer sequence $(1,\underbrace{2,2,\dots,2}_{(k-2)/2\ \text{twos}},1)$ is a most avoided pattern of length $k$, i.e. it minimizes $\mathrm{pd}(\tau)$ over $\tau\in S_k$.
artifact.status_search_result: No source located that proves or refutes the conjecture that, for even $k$, the layered pattern with layer sequence $(1,2,2,\dots,2,1)$ minimizes packing density among length-$k$ patterns. Recent works on packing densities and density maximizers of layered permutations do not report a resolution, so the conjecture appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Density maximizers of layered permutations (arXiv:2110.01723)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on densities of layered permutations and their maximizers, with no claim resolving the minimum-packing-density conjecture for even-length layered patterns (1,2,...,2,1).
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is not reported as resolved in current work on layered permutation packing.

status_evidence.title: On the Best Upper Bound for Permutations Avoiding a Pattern of a Given Length (arXiv:1209.2404)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses extremal questions for pattern avoidance of given length without refuting the layered (1,2,...,2,1) conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: No refutation of the Kézdy–Snevily layered conjecture is reported.
